thread:
maria (eng-infra): anyone seeing spike in 502/503 from edge-proxy -> gpu-pool in ap-southeast-2? started ~10:14Z, lots of targets failing healthchecks :grimacing:
jeff (eng-runtime): yep, alerts came in. ALB target group shows Failed health checks, 504s. edge-proxy logs show connection resets when talking to pod IPs.
kai (sre): pulling VPC flow logs /cloudtrail for that subnet now. can you paste an example request id from the proxy logs?
maria (eng-infra): req=7f2c2a9b, attached few lines from proxy log: "upstream connect error or disconnect, connection reset by peer". pushing the log snippet now.
edge-proxy-bot: [log] 2026-03-18T10:13:59Z req=7f2c2a9b "GET /v1/complete" 502 upstream reset from 10.0.45.12:37011
jeff (eng-runtime): flow logs show ALB ENI -> node TCP SYN on port 37011, node responds with RST. repeated. looks like return path is being blocked.
kai (sre): checking NACLs for the worker-subnet. I see a recent change (rule 110) that DENYs tcp ports 32768-65535 egress. That will drop ephemeral replies.
anika (eng-platform): who changed that NACL? I remember we tightened ephemeral egress for a different tenant last week.
jeff (eng-runtime): it was part of the "ingress hardening" change PR #5423 by ops last Thursday. intent was to block uncontrolled egress from dev nodes, but looks like those rules applied to the GPU worker subnet by mistake.
maria (eng-infra): great catch. need a quick mitigation, targets are draining. can we allow ephemeral ports temporarily?
kai (sre): yes, temp fix: allow ephemeral range for that NACL rule or add explicit allow for ALB source CIDR. I recommend opening ephemeral range outbound so established connections can complete.
deploy-bot: created incident INC-2026-342 and ticket TKT-8892. paging eng-infra on-call.
anika (eng-platform): prepping the CLI to patch NACL. command I'm about to run (dry-run):
```
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry \
  --network-acl-id acl-07a1b2c3d4e5f6789 \
  --rule-number 110 \
  --protocol 6 \
  --port-range From=32768,To=65535 \
  --egress false \
  --rule-action allow \
  --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0
```
kai (sre): that will work. also verify it doesn't open up dev-only subnets to the world; it only affects reply ports from nodes to ALB, which is fine for now.
jeff (eng-runtime): before patching, can we confirm ALB healthcheck source IPs? they're in the public ALB range but inside VPC 	6 better to allow ephemeral ports from the ALB security group too.
maria (eng-infra): done, running the replace command now. will monitor.
anika (eng-platform): applied change at 10:21Z. NACL acl-07a1b2c3d4e5f6789 rule 110 now set to ALLOW ephemeral range for ingress.
kai (sre): I'm seeing SYN/ACK succeeded now, node no longer RST'ing. Target group health passing 3/3 at 10:23Z :tada:
edge-proxy-bot: [metric] upstream_error_rate for req=7f2c2a9b dropping from 22% -> 0.5% over 2 minutes.
jeff (eng-runtime): rolling logs look good. cores/latency back to normal.
maria (eng-infra): good catch on the NACL rule mixup. action items: 1) revert the broad NACL tightening and apply correctly to dev-only subnets; 2) add a preflight test that verifies ALB->node ephemeral port connectivity when changing NACLs; 3) postmortem/TKT-8892
anika (eng-platform): adding RFC to infra-runbook and will scope a safer rule-change flow (apply tag-based filters + CI test).
deploy-bot: INC-2026-342 resolved at 10:28Z. TKT-8892 assigned to anika.
maria (eng-infra): thanks all 	6 services recovered. leaving follow-up items in the ticket. closing thread.
